C-FIX-TAP-POINTER-RECOVERY.IntentSummary: Let the interceptor recover from a release that never arrives, and take its tap threshold from the framework's device-aware slop, with a regression test for the exact sequence that caused permanent deafness.

MustPassCommand.Command: grep -q 'silent after a lost release\|after a lost release' .grace/verification/main.xml

T-001.Title: Recover from a lost release and use the device's own threshold

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A press arriving while a stale pointer is tracked adopts the new pointer instead of being ignored, so no sequence of events can silence the interceptor indefinitely.
Staleness is judged by the time since the tracked pointer was last heard from, and a mouse — which cannot be mid-gesture with a second pointer — is adopted on every press without waiting.
The drag threshold comes from computeHitSlop for the event's device kind, so a mouse press beyond its precise slop is not a tap while touch keeps the touch slop.
A genuine two-finger touch gesture still produces one sound, not two.

T-002.Title: Pin the lost release and the device threshold

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: A test sends a down whose up never arrives and then a genuine tap, and asserts the second press still clicks once — the sequence that proved the deafness.
A test drives a mouse-kind press that moves past the precise slop but far short of the touch slop and asserts silence, because the framework would not call that a tap either.
The existing tap, drag and sound-off tests keep passing unchanged.

T-003.Title: Record the recovery in the durable verification

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: V-M-SOUND states that a press whose release never arrives must not silence the presses that follow, and that the interceptor's threshold is the device-aware one the framework uses.
